subproblems.question: Quantify the scope of annual global HPC energy consumption under both full-capacity and average-utilization operation.
subproblems.deliverable: Global annual HPC (data-centre) electricity demand in 2024 with defensible lower/central/upper bounds for full-load and average-utilization cases.
hard_constraints: bounds must bracket published IEA value
facts: IEA: data centres consumed ~415 TWh in 2024 (~1.5% of global electricity)
servers draw substantial idle power, so energy-basis utilization is higher than compute utilization
assumptions: HPC scope = data-centre IT load (servers+AI+storage+network), PUE covers cooling+power overhead
crypto mining treated as optional add-on outside the IEA DC figure
ambiguities: HPC definition breadth (supercomputers only vs all data centres) -> adopt data-centre definition, state it
fleet capacity factor poorly measured -> propagate uncertainty

evidence.note: literature anchors with ranges and URLs

subproblems.question: Build a comprehensive model of total carbon emissions from HPC energy consumption, considering how energy is produced and the energy mix.
subproblems.deliverable: Carbon model C = E * CI(mix) with fuel-level emission factors derived from real generation data (Ember), regional disaggregation, Monte-Carlo uncertainty.
soft_objectives: regional disaggregation preferred over single global grid
facts: Ember 2024 world CI = 471 gCO2/kWh; coal 34.1%, gas 22.3% of world generation
assumptions: average (not marginal) grid intensity for annual accounting
DC distribution across regions from market-share estimates
out_of_scope: embodied carbon of hardware (handled qualitatively in Q5 link)
acceptance_criteria: C_2024 within defensible range (~150-260 Mt given 415 TWh x 350-600 g/kWh)
fuel factors reproducible from data_cleaned CSV

subproblems.question: Explore how the model changes as HPC grows, other sectors' energy demand rises, and energy resources/structure change; give realistic 2030 bounds.
subproblems.deliverable: Scenario projections 2025-2030 of HPC energy and emissions under conservative/baseline/high growth x grid decarbonization; 2030 bounds.
hard_constraints: anchored to at least two independent published projections
bounds must follow from scenarios, not a single point
soft_objectives: interactions between demand growth and grid decarbonization quantified
facts: IEA: 945 TWh by 2030 baseline (~3% of global electricity)
Goldman Sachs: +160% data-centre power demand by 2030
assumptions: constant-shape logistic/annual growth approximation between anchors
grid CI decay independent of DC demand in scenarios
acceptance_criteria: 2030 bounds bracket IEA 945 TWh baseline energy

subproblems.question: Simulate the impact of increasing the renewable share; compute corresponding carbon reductions; study 100% renewable potential and challenges.
subproblems.deliverable: Emissions vs clean-energy-share curve (2024 and 2030), marginal abatement per +10pp clean share, 100% renewable feasibility discussion.
hard_constraints: share sweep must be coherent (mix renormalization)
soft_objectives: identify which fossil fuel is displaced first (coal vs gas)
assumptions: proportional displacement of fossil share unless stated
lifecycle residual of clean fleet from Ember fuel-level data
ambiguities: storage/intermittency not endogenously modeled -> discussed qualitatively + firm-capacity constraint
acceptance_criteria: curve monotonic; 100% clean residual <10% of baseline

subproblems.question: Improve the model (or build a new one) for ONE key area beyond carbon; explain the choice and its link to energy consumption.
subproblems.deliverable: Water-usage extension: W(t) = E_IT(t) x WUE; scarcity weighting; 2024-2030 projections; energy-water nexus discussion.
inputs: WUE distribution (Google 1.8 L/kWh; Meta ~0.2; industry upper ~5)
hard_constraints: water model must consume energy model output (explicit coupling)
facts: cooling dominates DC water use; WUE spread across cooling technologies is >10x
assumptions: WUE constant within scenario; technology shift as sensitivity
ambiguities: withdrawal vs consumption accounting -> use consumption
acceptance_criteria: W_2024 within 0.3-0.8 km3 (plausible global range) for baseline WUE

subproblems.question: Actionable recommendations; incorporate one recommendation into the model; 1-2 page letter to the UN Advisory Board.
subproblems.deliverable: Recommendation set; one recommendation implemented as a model lever (carbon-aware scheduling lever reducing effective CI); letter to UN.
hard_constraints: recommendations must be actionable and technical+policy oriented
soft_objectives: lever shows measurable reduction under 2030 scenarios
facts: AI training workloads are deferrable/shiftable; CI varies diurnally by up to ~2x in solar-heavy grids
assumptions: average CI reduction from temporal shifting ~10-20% of grid CI
acceptance_criteria: lever reduces C_2030 by a quantified, defensible margin; letter references frozen numbers
